addresses: visual-phone, major: 'Sign out is now the lowest, largest-reach row on the screen... on a counselor's build there are no destinations above it: one wanted row sitting directly on top of one that ends her evening, 9px apart, with the destructive one nearer the thumb'

design-phone, minor: 'the loudest element in the whole panel is the destructive one... bring the identity back to a lightness that can be read at a glance... the three destinations should be what the sheet presents first'
changes.change: Sign out is no longer a row in the destination list. It moved into the identity block at the top of the surface, on the same line as the role chip, right-aligned: 'Signed in as / dana.ruiz@example.org / [ADMIN]  Sign out'. It keeps a 44px touch box (min-h-11, pointer-fine:min-h-8) and its danger colour, but at text-sm beside a chip rather than as a full-width 48px slab, so it is no longer what the sheet presents first. The identity itself came up the ramp to meet the second half of the finding: 'Signed in as' ink-600 to ink-500, the email ink-400 to ink-200 on its own full-width line, the role chip 10px/ink-500 to 11px/ink-400. The three destinations (one, for a counselor) are now the only rows, and they own the whole reachable band.
changes.rationale: Reach and consequence now point opposite ways: the destinations are the bottom 144px of the sheet, the irreversible item is at the top edge of a surface whose top edge is roughly 620px up an 844px screen. Attaching it to the identity is the reading the critic proposed and it is also true — signing out is an act on the account the block names, not a fourth place to go — which is why it survives on the pointer build too, where it costs nothing and stops a navigation popover from carrying its only chroma on its widest object. Putting the email on its own line rather than beside the button was forced by the 208px pointer popover, where a side-by-side identity truncated it to 'dana.ruiz@ex…'; the fact the panel is predicated on now reads in full at both widths.
changes.breakpoint: both — one item list, one order. Below lg it is the bottom sheet, at lg the popover; only the container differs, as before.
changes.implementation: src/components/AppShell.tsx, in the shared account-menu item list extracted in r01. The identity block becomes `<div className="border-b border-ink-800 px-4 pb-2 pt-1 pointer-fine:px-3">` holding `Signed in as` (text-xs ink-500), the email (`truncate text-xs text-ink-200`), then `<div className="mt-1 flex items-center justify-between gap-3">` with the role chip and the sign-out button (`-mr-2 flex min-h-11 items-center rounded-lg px-2 text-sm font-medium text-danger-400 hover:bg-ink-800 pointer-fine:min-h-8`). Delete the `mt-1 border-t border-ink-800 pt-1 pb-2` wrapper that used to hold it at the foot.

addresses: visual-phone, major: 'the counselor's version is in no frame in either round... render the counselor's open sheet as a frame; it is the surface the whole "whoever you are" half of this journey now rests on'
changes.change: New pair of prototypes, kiosk-menu-counselor--phone.html and --desktop.html: the account menu open, for a counselor, over the counselor's own pair-kiosk page. Exactly what `can('core')` removes is removed — the Team and Settings rows — and exactly what it does not is kept: Kiosk, because /pair-kiosk is ungated, and Sign out. The shell is the rail-less one from kiosk-setup-counselor: no aside, no tab bar, header rendered at every width with its contents on the page column's measure, main without pb-24. At lg the menu is the popover under the header chip (hidden lg:block); below lg it is the same bottom sheet the admin gets (lg:hidden), scrim included.
changes.rationale: Two rounds judged this surface by subtracting rows from a picture of the admin's, and the subtraction is where the ordering fault lived: with three destinations gone, whatever sits last is unavoidably first under the thumb. Now it is a frame, and the frame shows the answer to that — one destination in the reachable band and the irreversible item at the far edge. The rail-less shell needs two DOM instances of one item list (sheet below lg, popover at lg) exactly as the admin shell already needs two (header and rail), so this is not a new pattern.
changes.breakpoint: both — the file is one document shot at two widths, like every other pair in this scene
changes.implementation: AppShell.tsx already gates Team and Settings behind `can('core')` and leaves the kiosk row ungated, so no item logic changes. What is new is that the rail-less shell must render the account menu itself: the header instance renders the portalled bottom sheet `lg:hidden` and, when no rail exists, also the `hidden lg:block` popover anchored to the header chip (`absolute right-0 z-20 mt-2 w-52 rounded-xl`). When a rail exists the header instance keeps rendering the sheet only, and the rail keeps its upward popover.

addresses: design-phone, major: 'the rank inside the form is inverted... the field it is waiting on is the faintest object in its own group... six ink-700 dots almost the same value as the ring around them'

design-desktop, major: 'the field won size and lost presence... give the field the presence instead, so the invitation sits on the thing that is actually live... the rank in this row should be field first, button second, at rest as well as after typing'
design-phone, major: 'settle the two objects' widths: a 210px field stacked over a 358px button leaves a stepped edge and a dead rectangle beside the field'
changes.change: Three moves inside the group, no new elements. The field steps toward the reader: fill ink-900 to ink-800, ring ink-700 to ink-600, placeholder dots ink-700 to ink-400, so it is a lit surface with six legible slots rather than an inert well. The resting primary steps back without losing its hue: disabled fill brand-500/20 to brand-500/10 and label brand-200 to brand-300. And the widths settle by breakpoint: below lg the field is full-measure like the button above it (the code shape is carried by 30px centred mono at 0.2em tracking, not by the box), at lg it keeps `lg:max-w-[7em]` so the field-and-button row is unchanged on a pointer. The label also stopped being the smallest type in its own group: it holds text-sm at both widths (the `pointer-fine:text-xs` step is gone) and moved ink-300 to ink-200.
changes.rationale: The inversion r01 fixed was a fill, and so is this one — but at the other end. Neither critic wanted the disabled primary neutralised again, so presence was bought on the live control and sold on the waiting one; the field is now the largest, lightest, most contrasted object below the lede at both widths, and the button is a tinted rectangle that becomes solid the moment six characters exist. Dropping the field's phone-width cap is what removes the stepped edge and the dead rectangle beside it, and it costs nothing on the phone: at 358px, a centred six-glyph monospace at 0.2em cannot read as free text or search, which was the objection that produced the cap in the first place — and that objection was measured at 1119px, where the cap still applies.
changes.breakpoint: both for the fill, ring, placeholder, label and button. Field width is a split: full measure below lg, 7em at lg and up.
changes.implementation: src/components/ui/Field.tsx, the `code` size preset from r01: `w-full rounded-xl bg-ink-800 px-4 py-3 text-center font-mono text-3xl tracking-[0.2em] text-ink-50 ring-1 ring-ink-600 placeholder:text-ink-400 lg:max-w-[7em]`, and the label class loses `pointer-fine:text-xs` and moves to `text-ink-200`. src/components/ui/Button.tsx: the primary's disabled clause becomes `disabled:bg-brand-500/10 disabled:text-brand-300 disabled:opacity-100`.

addresses: visual-phone, minor: 'it reserves one line for a message the ideation itself specifies at two, so the ten-minute hint under it still jumps when the verdict arrives, and the verdict is set at exactly the same 14px as that hint'

design-phone, minor: 'the reserved slot is the right idea in the wrong place in the rhythm... it reads as a stray paragraph floating between the form and the divider... the resting state should show the same grouping the populated state will'
changes.change: The empty reserved line is gone and the hint is now the live region. One paragraph under the button, `id="…-hint" aria-live="polite"`, holds the ten-minute sentence at rest and is replaced in place by the verdict after a submit — at text-base font-semibold ink-100, a size step above the text-sm ink-400 it replaces.
changes.rationale: The two findings pull against each other only if the slot has to be empty: reserve enough height for a 65-character sentence and the resting page carries a 48px hole that groups with nothing. It does not have to be empty, because the pre-submit hint and the post-submit verdict are the same sentence at two moments — 'codes last ten minutes, read the one showing now and try again' is precisely what a refusal has to say, and a success replaces advice that no longer applies. So one element, always populated, never a hole, and the arrival is a swap at a size step up rather than an insertion that pushes. It also shrinks rather than grows: the idle hint sets to three lines at 390px, the success sentence to two. Wording stays bounded by what the server confirms — 'Code ABC123 approved — the kiosk signs itself in on its next poll', never 'the kiosk is signed in'.
changes.implementation:
KioskPage.tsx PairCard: delete the separate outcome paragraph. The hint element becomes the outcome element — one `

` whose text is the outcome when there is one and the hint otherwise, and whose class switches from `max-w-prose text-sm leading-snug text-ink-400` to `max-w-prose text-base font-semibold leading-snug text-ink-100`. `aria-describedby` on the input keeps pointing at it, which is what makes the result the field's description after a submit.

addresses: visual-desktop, major: '"Check again" arrived, but nothing on the page reports back when the answer does not change... the admin cannot tell "checked again, still refused" from "the button did nothing"... in the healthy frame there is not even a slot for a reply'
design-phone, minor: 'the badge has inherited the exact costume of the page's outline buttons... the chip invites a tap that does nothing'
design-phone, minor: 'three facts, three different left edges for their values... the service account breaks mid-identifier'
design-desktop, minor: 'five kinds of content at one uniform 8px gap, so nothing groups... the facts row is wedged between the sentence that says grant it and the command that grants it'
visual-phone, minor (denied): 'the remedy did not move at all... the command block begins exactly where the sticky tab bar starts'
changes.change: The deployment block was re-cut, identically in both states. The verdict stopped being a chip: 'Ready to pair' is now text-sm semibold ink-100 and 'Cannot sign kiosk tokens' text-sm semibold danger-400, plain type on the page, so nothing in the block wears an outline except the things that respond to a tap. 'Checked' left the fact row and became the re-check's reply: an `aria-live` paragraph with `min-h-8` directly under the Check again button, reading 'Checked 6:41 pm' at rest and the verdict-with-time after a click. The order is now verdict, explanation, remedy, actions, identifying facts — so on the denied page the gcloud block and its two buttons sit directly under the sentence that tells you to run them, about 90px higher than before, and the project facts land after the diagnosis instead of inside it. The facts themselves became a two-item list with terms above values, one value edge, full measure for the service account, and they group by gap (gap-3 between kinds, gap-1 and gap-2 within) rather than one uniform 8px.
changes.rationale: The re-check's whole purpose is the thirty-to-a-hundred-and-twenty seconds while an IAM grant propagates, when the honest answer is 'still no' — so the reply has to be legible when it is identical, which means it has to be next to the button and it has to carry the time. Making it the same element in both states also gives the healthy block the slot it had no reason to lack. Demoting the verdict from a pill to type is what stops it reading as a control; it also lets the accent do its r01 job — danger is still the only chroma in the block, and it now appears as a sentence rather than as a red button. Moving the facts to the end is what the desktop critic asked for and what the phone critic's 'lift the remedy' resolves to: the identifiers are confirmation you check once, the command is the errand.
changes.breakpoint: both — the fact list runs as a column below lg and a row at lg, which it already did; everything else is unconditional
changes.implementation:
KioskPage.tsx SigningCard. Drop `` for a `

`. Section becomes `flex flex-col gap-3` with an inner `flex flex-col gap-1` (verdict + explanation) and, when not ok, an inner `flex flex-col gap-2` (pre + button row). Render `

` after the actions in both states, fed by `dataUpdatedAt` and the last verdict. The `dl` becomes `flex flex-col gap-2 lg:flex-row lg:gap-8` with each pair `flex flex-col gap-0.5`, dt ink-500, dd ink-200, and no `break-words`; the 'Checked' pair is deleted from it.

addresses: visual-desktop, major: 'the state most admins will actually meet is this one — the deployment is fine and the lobby screen is still stuck... the only block that addresses the question says "it says nothing about the screen in the lobby" and stops... the answers are already on the page and in the journey but scattered in three different registers'
design-desktop, minor: 'the two columns' terminal controls miss each other by 14px'
changes.change: A third section under the rule, 'If the kiosk still waits', holding the three causes that are already known and true, as a list: a code expires ten minutes after the kiosk shows it; a kiosk installed to the device's home screen keeps its own storage and asks to be paired a second time; a kiosk stops when its approver's access is deactivated. It sits immediately to the right of the deployment block at lg, stacked under it below lg, sharing the last third of the grid with Phone search. The third of these facts used to be the opening clause of a footer paragraph, which now begins 'To retire a kiosk, clear the browser's site data…' — the fact moved, it was not duplicated.
changes.rationale: This is the journey's second job answered where the person actually arrives with it, and it is a regrouping rather than a new claim: every line is something the app or the journey already states, and none of them says anything about the lobby screen being fine. It goes beside the deployment block because that block's last sentence is the disclaimer that raises the question — 'it says nothing about the screen in the lobby' now has the next column as its answer, which is why the caveat stays verbatim where it is instead of being borrowed as a heading. Putting it in the third column with Phone search rather than in the 568px of empty upper-right also keeps r01's register split intact: one job above the rule, references below it. The 14px baseline miss dissolves on the way: Check again and Rebuild are no longer peers at the same height in adjacent columns.
changes.breakpoint: both for the content; at lg it is column three, below lg it stacks
changes.implementation: KioskPage.tsx: wrap StuckKioskCard and PhoneIndexCard in a `<div className="flex flex-col gap-6">` inside the existing `lg:grid lg:grid-cols-3` region, so the grid has two children (SigningCard at `lg:col-span-2`, the pair at column three). The new section is a static `<ul className="flex flex-col gap-2 text-xs leading-relaxed text-ink-400">` under the same `text-xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wide text-ink-500` heading the other two use — core-team only, in the same guarded region, since a counselor never sees this half of the page. Trim the first clause of the retirement paragraph.

addresses: design-phone, minor: 'the subordinate register is set by the headings only; the bodies underneath do not keep the promise — 14px ink-500 under one, 12px ink-500 under the other, 14px ink-300 in the denied frame'

design-desktop, minor: 'fix one body size for the whole subordinate register so peer sections read as peers, and let a single step of contrast distinguish a fact you may need to act on from the small print... if the footer is a lower rank it should look lower rather than identical'
changes.change: One body size below the rule — `text-xs leading-relaxed` for every paragraph and list in the register — and three steps of contrast doing the ranking instead of size: ink-300 for the thing you have to act on (the denied explanation), ink-400 for the register's ordinary body (the healthy caveat, the troubleshooting list, the phone-search description), ink-500 for the footer small print under the second rule. Fact values sit at ink-200, brighter than any of it, because they are identifiers to be compared character by character.
changes.rationale: The register was announced by its headings and then contradicted by four different body treatments, so it read as four unrelated blocks that happened to share a label style. Holding one size makes the sections peers; the contrast ramp is then free to say something true — act on this, read this if you need it, this is background — and the footer finally looks like a lower rank than the live utility above it instead of being typographically the same thing. The denied explanation keeps the top of the ramp rather than stepping the whole block up to full voice, because the full-voice statement of that fault is already above the field, where the reader meets it before typing.
changes.implementation: KioskPage.tsx: SigningCard's caveat and PhoneIndexCard's paragraph become `max-w-prose text-xs leading-relaxed text-ink-400`; the denied explanation `max-w-prose text-xs leading-relaxed text-ink-300`; the two footer paragraphs keep `text-xs leading-relaxed text-ink-500`; `dd` values move ink-300 to ink-200.

addresses: visual-desktop, minor: 'break-words split the line inside the service account identifier... an admin who retypes this has a fair chance of producing "tally- 76406@…" or dropping the hyphen'
changes.change: The command is now written with shell continuations, one whole flag per line: `gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding tally-76406 \` / `  --member=serviceAccount:… \` / `  --role=roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator`. Three lines instead of two, chosen by a person rather than by the browser; at 1440 no identifier is split and the block is one line taller.
changes.rationale: A line break inside a service account identifier is a grant that fails for a reason the reader is not looking for, and the copy button only helps on the machine showing the page — which, for gcloud, is rarely the same machine. Backslash continuations are what a person would paste anyway, so the block is now retypable as well as copyable. `whitespace-pre-wrap break-words` stays, because at 390px the 62-character member flag cannot fit any way and the alternative is silent horizontal clipping, which was r01's blocker; on a phone the copy button is the answer and the wrap is honest about not fitting.
changes.breakpoint: both — the string is the same; only at lg does it stop wrapping
changes.implementation: KioskPage.tsx: the command template literal gains ` \\\n  ` between arguments. Keep `whitespace-pre-wrap break-words` on the `pre` and keep the copy button beside it.

addresses: design-desktop, minor: 'the banner and the pre inset their text 12px, so text starts at x=256 for everything else and at x=268 for the two tinted panels — on the one screen whose composition is "the content is the page", nothing should start in a second place'
changes.change: The pre-submit warning lost its panel: no fill, no ring, no padding — it is a `max-w-prose text-sm text-danger-400` paragraph between the lede and the field label, marked by accent and position alone. The gcloud block keeps its surface, because a command wants one, but hangs its padding outside the measure (`-mx-3 px-3`), so its first character sits on the page's left edge like everything else.
changes.rationale: Both offered remedies were right for different elements. A sentence of red type directly above the field is if anything a stronger warning than a red box, and dropping the box also thins out the denied page's alarm count — the field is no longer a silent trough between two tinted panels, which was half of the desktop major about the pairing row. The command block is the one thing on the page that genuinely is a different substance from the prose, so it keeps its fill and gives up its indent instead.
changes.implementation: KioskPage.tsx: the warning paragraph drops `rounded-xl bg-danger-500/10 px-3 py-2 ring-1 ring-danger-500/25`, keeping `max-w-prose text-sm text-danger-400`. The `pre` gains `-mx-3`.

addresses: design-phone, minor: 'they are twins: same full width, same height, same radius, same semibold label... at a squint the lower one is the more legible of the two... one lone button given 24px above and below and a hairline on each side becomes a titled section without a title'
design-desktop, minor: 'two rules 86px apart fence off a mostly empty band around a single small button... this role's only route onward is weighted like a maintenance utility'
changes.change: The exit is no longer a slab and no longer bracketed. The rule above it is gone, and it is now a link-weight control — `✓ Check in` in brand-300 at text-base, no fill, no ring, with a 48px touch box (min-h-12, pointer-fine:min-h-9) — sitting as the closing move of the page before the footer rule. One rule remains on the counselor's page and it introduces something.
changes.rationale: Twins were the problem and a lesser twin would still be a twin, so the exit changed class: a destination, in the app's own blue, reading as a way onward rather than as a second thing to press. That also separates it from the outline maintenance buttons the desktop critic did not want it grouped with — it is neither a primary nor a utility. Brand-300 is the existing link colour family (the wordmark is brand-400); no new accent enters. Dropping the rule removes the section-without-a-title without needing to invent a heading for a single link.
changes.breakpoint: both. The exit itself is scoped to the rail-less shell — a counselor on any screen that is not check-in — not to a width.
changes.implementation: KioskPage.tsx: when `!core`, render `<Link to="/" className="inline-flex min-h-12 items-center gap-2 text-base font-medium text-brand-300 hover:text-brand-200 pointer-fine:min-h-9 pointer-fine:text-sm">` in a bare `<div>`, with no `border-t`/`pt-6` wrapper.

addresses: design-desktop, minor: 'the header pads by 16px and the page by 32px, so the wordmark starts 32px left of the h1 and the chip ends 32px right of the text column — the frame looks like it slipped rather than like it was set'
changes.change: The rail-less header's inner wrapper now carries the page column's padding rather than the bar's: the bar is `px-4 lg:px-0` and the wrapper is `max-w-lg lg:max-w-2xl lg:px-8`. At 1440 the wordmark's left edge and the h1's left edge are both x=416, and the chip's right edge matches the column's.
changes.rationale: The two elements agreed on a max-width and disagreed on padding, which is the worst of both — a near-miss reads as a slip where an open difference would read as a decision. Matching after padding at both widths costs one class and leaves the bar full-bleed, so the chrome still spans the window while its contents belong to the page.
changes.breakpoint: lg and up; below lg both resolve to a 16px inset already and nothing moves
changes.implementation: AppShell.tsx, the rail-less header branch: `className="… px-4 py-2 pt-safe backdrop-blur lg:px-0"` on the `<header>`, and `mx-auto flex w-full max-w-lg items-center justify-between gap-3 lg:max-w-2xl lg:px-8` on the wrapper — the same padding scale PageFrame uses.

addresses: visual-phone, minor: 'the sheet behind it is now a 48px-row surface in the thumb zone, but the door to it was left at 32px in the corner the brief names as unreachable... the whole growth needed is 8px of vertical padding on touch'
changes.change: The account chip gets `min-h-11 pointer-fine:min-h-8` in both shell slots — 44px on touch, its current 32px on a pointer.
changes.rationale: Cheap, obviously right, and the same `pointer-fine` split the sheet rows already use, so the pointer build is untouched and a touch laptop gets the bigger target. 44 rather than 48 because the chip lives inside a header bar whose height is set by its own padding; 48 would deepen the bar on every screen in the app for a control that is tapped once per journey.
changes.breakpoint: touch only (`pointer-fine` reverts it), at every width
changes.implementation: AppShell.tsx: add `min-h-11 … pointer-fine:min-h-8` to the account chip button class, which is shared by the header and rail instances.

declined.finding: design-desktop, minor: 'the page is composed at two widths and the wider one belongs to the reference material... either the subordinate register comes in to the measure the job occupies, or the job register earns the full width. A rule should not be wider than the wider of the two things it divides.'
declined.why: Declined, and it is the one finding this round argues with. The register below the rule is now genuinely three columns of content and is 1399px wide; the rule is 1407. It is not wider than what it divides — it is wider than what is *above* it, which is a form that receives six characters and has no business being 1152px. Bringing the register in to the form's 668px would undo r01's density change and push the deployment facts, the troubleshooting list and the utility below the fold to buy an alignment nobody is blocked by. The rule reads as the boundary of a full-width region, which is what it is.

declined.finding: visual-phone, minor (denied): 'the command block begins exactly where the sticky tab bar starts, so at rest it is entirely behind opaque chrome' — the remedy should be one tap from where the reader's eye stopped.
declined.why: Half-taken. The command and its two buttons moved above the project facts, which lifts them about 90px: at 390×844 the `pre` now starts around y=690 and the buttons straddle the tab bar's top edge instead of sitting 106px below it. The rest is arithmetic that cannot be won without deleting content the same critics asked for — the lede, the danger sentence, a 60px field, a 48px button and the hint are 640px before the rule. A flick still finishes the job, which is what made it minor.

declined.finding: visual-desktop, minor (implied): the gcloud command still breaks inside the service account identifier at 390px.
declined.why: Not fixable at that width and not worth faking. The member flag is 62 characters; fitting it would need a ~9px monospace, and the alternative — `whitespace-pre` with `overflow-x-auto` — is the silent clipping that was round one's blocker on this element. On a phone the copy button is the honest answer; the finding was raised about retyping on a machine that has gcloud, and that machine is at 1440, where the break is now gone.

declined.finding: design-phone, minor: 'let the status stop being a chip, or let the buttons stop being rings' — in this block only the things that respond to a tap should have an outline.
declined.why: Taken, but only the first half: the verdict stopped being a chip. The outline buttons keep their rings, because they are the round-1 answer to a different finding (the maintenance controls out-shouting the primary) and because a ring is how this page distinguishes a secondary control from body text now that the cards are gone. With no other ringed object in the block, the ring means pressable again.

declined.finding: visual-desktop, major (residue): the counselor's denied state — 'this will not work, ask a leader' with no project detail.
declined.why: Still not a frame, for the same reason as in r01: a counselor never receives `getKioskStatus` (the server refuses it below core), so their denied state exists only as a submit failure and no frame in this round is post-submit. It is specified — the shared outcome paragraph carries 'Approved, but this kiosk cannot be signed in — ask a core team member to check kiosk setup' — and the element it lands in is now the always-present hint slot, so there is nothing left to build for it.
